source_text:
Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (homilia 4) (e cod. Sinaitico gr. 492)
Τοῦ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πάσχα
1 Σάλπιγξ ἡμῖν ἱερὰ καὶ βασιλικὴ τὸ πνευματικὸν τοῦτο συνεκρότησεν
θέατρον, σάλπιγξ ἣν ἐπλήρωσεν Βηθλεὲμ καὶ ἡ Σιὼν ἐπύρωσεν, ἐν ᾗ ὁ Σταυρὸς
σφῦρα καὶ ἄκμων ἡ Ἀνάστασις. Ἧς οὐκ οἶδα πῶς ἐξείπω τὸ κάλλος, πῶς ἐκφράσω τὸ
φῶς, πῶς μηνύσω τὴν ἐν αὐτῷ χαράν, πῶς τὴν ἐν αὐτῇ βασιλείαν διηγήσωμαι. Ποίᾳ
δὲ αὐτὴν ψηλαφήσω χειρί;
2 Ποίοις λόγοις ἀσπάσομαι τάφον γεννῶντα ζωήν, μνῆμα φθορᾶς <μὲν>
ἐλεύθερον, ἀφθαρσίας δὲ πρόξενον, παστάδα τριή μερον τὸν νυμφίον κοιμήσασαν,
νυμφῶνα τὴν νύμφην ἄφθορον μετὰ γάμον ἐγείραντα; Νεκρὸν ἡ θήκη φυλαττομένη
καὶ θεὸν ἡ γῆ σαλευομένη· νεκρὸν μὲν γὰρ αὐτὸν τὸ σῶμα βοᾷ, τὸ δὲ θαῦμα θεόν·
νεκρὸν ἡ ταφή, θεὸν ἡ ἀνάστασις· νεκρὸν τῶν γυναικῶν καὶ τὰ δάκρυα, καὶ θεὸν
τῶν ἀγγέλων τὰ ῥήματα. Ὡς νεκρὸν αὐτὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἐκήδευσεν, ἀλλ' ὁ κηδευθεὶς ὡς
thought_title: The holy trumpet gathers the spiritual theater of Easter
orientation: Hesychius opens the homily by describing the Easter trumpet that assembles the spiritual theater, filled by Bethlehem and fired by Zion, with the Cross as hammer and Resurrection as anvil, and confesses the impossibility of declaring its beauty, light, joy, and kingdom.
pass_a_gloss: A holy and royal trumpet for us gathered together this spiritual theater, a trumpet which Bethlehem filled and Zion fired, in which the Cross is the hammer and the Resurrection the anvil. Of which I do not know how to speak out the beauty, how to declare the light, how to make known the joy in it, how to narrate the kingdom in it. With what hand shall I touch it? With what words shall I greet a tomb begetting life, a tombstone free of corruption but a procurator of incorruptibility, a bridal chamber having put the bridegroom to sleep for three parts of a day, a bridal chamber having raised the bride incorruptible after marriage? The coffin guarded him as dead and the earth shook as God; for the body cries out that he is dead, but the miracle declares God; the burial says dead, the Resurrection says God; the tears of the women say dead, and the words of the angels say God. Joseph buried him as dead, but the one buried as a man...

choices.english: a holy and royal trumpet for us
choices.why: Dative ἡμῖn indicates benefit/reference; 'for us' kept plain, not 'our'.
συνκροτέω = assemble/gather; 'theater' kept literal as the metaphor for the liturgical assembly.
Cross = hammer, Resurrection = anvil; retain the tool imagery without smoothing.

choices.term: μνῆμα φθορᾶς <μὲν> ἐλεύθερον, ἀφθαρσίας δὲ πρόξενον
choices.english: a tombstone free of corruption but a procurator of incorruptibility
choices.why: φθορά = corruption; ἐλεύθερον = free; πρόξενος = procurator/agent; keep the legal/forensic tone.
rejected: a memorial free from decay and a bringer of incorruption

choices.english: having put to sleep / having raised
choices.why: Aorist participles keep the completed action; 'put to sleep' for κοιμάω (bury), 'raised' for ἐγείρω.

choices.term: νεκρὸν μὲν γὰρ αὐτὸν τὸ σῶμα βοᾷ, τὸ δὲ θαῦμα θεόν
choices.english: for the body cries out that he is dead, but the miracle declares God
choices.why: μέν…δέ contrast; βοᾷ = cries out; θαῦμα = miracle; keep the two witnesses (body, miracle).
rejected: for his body cries out dead, but the wonder God

pass_b_english: A holy and royal trumpet for us gathered together this spiritual theater. Bethlehem filled it, and Zion fired it. In it the Cross is the hammer and the Resurrection the anvil. I do not know how to utter its beauty, how to express its light, how to declare the joy within it, or how to recount the kingdom within it. With what hand shall I even touch it?

In what words shall I greet a tomb that begets life, a grave free of corruption yet a procurator of incorruptibility, a bridal chamber that put the Bridegroom to sleep for three days and raised the bride undefiled after the wedding? The tomb under guard proclaimed a dead man, and the earth, shaken, proclaimed God. For his body cries out that he is dead, but the miracle declares God. The burial proclaims him dead, the Resurrection proclaims God. The women's tears treat him as dead, yet the angels' words proclaim God. Joseph buried him as a dead man, yet the one buried
notes: The source text ends mid-sentence at 'ὁ κηδευθεὶς ὡς'; the next word 'ἄνθρωπος' begins the following section.

problems.quote: The coffin guarded him as a dead man, yet the earth shook as God.
problems.source_quote: Νεκρὸν ἡ θήκη φυλαττομένη καὶ θεὸν ἡ γῆ σαλευομένη
problems.why: φυλαττομένη is passive: the tomb is the thing being guarded. The English makes the coffin the guard. The parallel with the shaken earth is lost, and so is the implied proclamation of 'dead' and 'God'.
problems.fix: The tomb under guard proclaims a dead man, and the earth, shaken, proclaims God.

problems.quote: raised the bride incorruptible after the wedding
problems.source_quote: τὴν νύμφην ἄφθορον μετὰ γάμον ἐγείραντα
problems.why: ἄφθορον means undefiled or uncorrupted, not made incorruptible (ἀφθαρσία).
problems.fix: a bridal chamber that raised the bride undefiled after the wedding
problems.ruling: ἄφθορον means undefiled/uncorrupted (virgin bride); 'incorruptible' imports ἀφθαρσία, and 'raised' after the wedding obscures the sense of unspoiled.

edits.old: The coffin guarded him as a dead man, yet the earth shook as God.
edits.new: The tomb under guard proclaimed a dead man, and the earth, shaken, proclaimed God.

edits.old: a bridal chamber that put the Bridegroom to sleep for three days and raised the bride incorruptible after the wedding
edits.new: a bridal chamber that put the Bridegroom to sleep for three days and raised the bride undefiled after the wedding

fixed: Changed 'The coffin guarded him as a dead man' to 'The tomb under guard proclaimed a dead man' to reflect passive φυλαττομένη and parallel with shaken earth; changed 'raised the bride incorruptible' to 'raised the bride undefiled' to match ἄφθορον (undefiled/uncorrupted) rather than ἀφθαρσία (incorruptibility).

last_rejected.why: πρόξενος means patron or provider, not a Roman procurator.
last_rejected.fix: a grave free of corruption, yet a patron of incorruptibility
last_rejected.ruling: πρόξενον means one who procures or provides. 'Procurator' is an odd word, but its sense of agent still approximates 'one who brings about'. This is a stylistic preference.

last_rejected.quote: a bridal chamber that put the Bridegroom to sleep for three days and raised the bride undefiled after the wedding
last_rejected.source_quote: παστάδα τριή μερον τὸν νυμφίον κοιμήσασαν, νυμφῶνα τὴν νύμφην ἄφθορον μετὰ γάμον ἐγείραντα
last_rejected.why: Two chambers: the παστάς laid him to sleep; the νυμφών raised the bride.
last_rejected.fix: a bridal chamber that laid the Bridegroom to sleep for three days, and a bride-room that raised the bride undefiled after the wedding
last_rejected.ruling: παστάδα (…κοιμήσασαν) and νυμφῶνα (…ἐγείραντα) are two nouns, so the English merges them. The agents are still chambers doing both acts, so the meaning is unchanged and the problem is minor.
